title: Separate file-hygiene rules
explanation: One rule per property: a tab anywhere, a 2-space indentation unit in code and HTML, and a filename with a space or a non-ASCII character. The rules are narrow, so the comparison can name exactly what each one covers.

cases.original: Use 4-space indents in code and Markdown when the format supports configurable indentation.
cases.note: The rule reads the leading-space unit of a file. Markdown is excluded because its indentation is structural.
cases.suggestion: Name the file types the rule covers, and say whether HTML indentation counts as code.

cases.original: Use spaces where the format allows a choice.
cases.note: A tab anywhere in the file is the violation. The rule does not distinguish a tab in a literal from one in indentation.
cases.suggestion: Say "no tab characters" rather than "use spaces".

cases.original: free of spaces and non-ASCII characters.
cases.note: Checked against the file name only.
cases.suggestion: Say "filenames contain no spaces or non-ASCII characters" in one sentence.
